questions.question: The sides AB and AC of ΔABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠ BCE meet at P. If ∠ A = 88°, the measure of ∠ P is :
questions.questionHtml: The sides AB and AC of ΔABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 88°, the measure of ∠P is :
questions.solution:
Given:

∠A = 88º

Concept used:

If P is the meeting point of bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE. Then, ∠P = \(1\over 2\) (180º - ∠A)

Calculation:

Substituting the value of A

⇒ ∠P = \(1\over 2\) (180º - 88º)

⇒ ∠P = \(1\over 2\) (92º) = 46º

Hence, the value of ∠P is 46º.

questions.question: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
questions.questionHtml: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
questions.solution:
Using Pythagoras theorem in triangles PTQ and PTR:

PQ2 = PT2 + QT2

QR = 2 × QT

Using Pythagoras theorem in ∆PTQ:

 

PQ2 = PT2 + QT2

⇒ 172 = 152 + QT2

⇒ QT2 = 64

⇒ QT = 8 cm

QR = 2 × QT

⇒ QR = 16 cm

questions.question: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 80 cm. If the side that is not equal in length to any of the other two sides is 20 cm, find the length of each of the equal sides.
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 80 cm. If the side that is not equal in length to any of the other two sides is 20 cm, find the length of each of the equal sides.
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Perimeter = 80 cm.

length of an unequal side = 20 cm.

FORMULA USED:

P = 2a + b  units.       Where P = Perimeter, a = length of two equal sides. and b = length of  base or unequal side.

CALCULATION:

Here P = 80 cm ,   b = 20 cm 

⇒P = 2a + b 

⇒ 80 = 2a + 20 

⇒2a = 60 

⇒ a = 30 cm.

Hence, Length of each of the equal sides is 30 cm.

questions.question: If in triangle ABC, D is a point on the side BC such that the line joining AD bisects the angle A. If the length of BD and BC are 4 cm and 10 cm respectively, then find the ratio of the lengths of AB and AC.
questions.questionHtml: If in triangle ABC, D is a point on the side BC such that the line joining AD bisects the angle A. If the length of BD and BC are 4 cm and 10 cm respectively, then find the ratio of the lengths of AB and AC.
questions.solution:
Given:

If in triangle ABC, D is a point on the side BC such that the line joining AD bisects the angle A.

The length of BD and BC are 4 cm and 10 cm respectively.

Concept used:

The Angle Bisector Theorem states that in a triangle, the angle bisector of a vertex divides the opposite side into segments that are proportional to the lengths of the other two sides.

Calculation:

DC = BC - BD = 10 - 4 = 6 cm

According to the concept,

Since AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, AB : AC = BD : DC

So, AB : AC

⇒ 4 : 6 = 2 : 3

∴ The ratio of the lengths of AB and AC is 2 : 3.

Since ∆ABC ≅ ∆QPR, the corresponding sides and angles will be equal. Hence, we identify the corresponding parts:

AB corresponds to PQ, AC corresponds to PR, and BC corresponds to QR.

Also, ∠A corresponds to ∠Q, ∠B corresponds to ∠P, and ∠C corresponds to ∠R.

questions.question: ∆ABC and ∆PQR are similar. The areas of these two triangles are 289 sq.cm and 576 sq.cm, respectively. If PR = 12 cm, then AC = ?
questions.questionHtml: ∆ABC and ∆PQR are similar. The areas of these two triangles are 289 sq.cm and 576 sq.cm, respectively. If PR = 12 cm, then AC = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

∆ABC and ∆PQR are similar.

Area of ∆ABC = 289 sq.cm

Area of ∆PQR = 576 sq.cm

PR = 12 cm

Formula used:

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Calculation:

Let AC be the corresponding side of PR in ∆ABC.

\(\dfrac{Area of ∆ABC}{Area of ∆PQR} = \left(\dfrac{AC}{PR}\right)^2 \)

\(\dfrac{289}{576} = \left(\dfrac{AC}{12}\right)^2 \)

⇒ \(\left(\dfrac{AC}{12}\right)^2 = \dfrac{289}{576} \)

⇒ \(AC = 12 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{289}{576}} \)

⇒ \(AC = 12 \times \dfrac{17}{24}\)

⇒ \(AC = 8.5 \)

∴ The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: ABC is an equilateral triangle. P, Q, and R are the mid-points of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively. If the length of the side of the triangle ABC is 11 cm, then the area (in cm 2 ) of \(\triangle\) PQR is:
questions.questionHtml: ABC is an equilateral triangle. P, Q, and R are the mid-points of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively. If the length of the side of the triangle ABC is 11 cm, then the area (in cm2) of \(\triangle\)PQR is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The triangle formed by joining the mid-points of the sides of any triangle has exactly 1/4th the area of the original triangle.

Area of original equilateral ΔABC = (√3 ÷ 4) × side2

Area of ΔABC = (√3 ÷ 4) × 112 = 121√3 ÷ 4 cm2

Area of ΔPQR = (1 ÷ 4) × Area of ΔABC = (1 ÷ 4) × (121√3 ÷ 4)

Area of ΔPQR = 121√3 / 16 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 121√3 / 16 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral ΔABC = 11 cm.

P, Q, and R are the mid-points of sides AB, BC, and CA respectively.

Formula Used:

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a2 (where a is the side length).

Calculations:

⇒ By the Mid-point Theorem, the line segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is half the length of the third side.

⇒ Side of equilateral ΔPQR = 11 ÷ 2 cm.

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = (√3 ÷ 4) × (11 ÷ 2)2

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = (√3 ÷ 4) × (121 ÷ 4)

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = 121√3 / 16 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 121√3 / 16 cm2.

Additional Information

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half as long as that third side.

Area Division by Midpoints

The triangle formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of any triangle divides the original triangle into four smaller congruent triangles of exactly equal area.

Equilateral Triangle Properties

In an equilateral triangle, all sides are equal and all internal angles are 60°. Its height (altitude) is given by (√3 ÷ 2) × side.

questions.question: Among the following options, which are NOT sides of a triangle?

questions.solution:
Given:

Four sets of three side lengths are given.

Formula used:

For a given triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must be greater than the third side.

Calculation:

Option 1: 12 + 9 > 15, 12 +15 > 9, 15 + 9 > 12. Therefore, the given three lengths are the sides of a triangle. 

Option 2: 20 + 20 > 20. Therefore, the given three lengths are the sides of a triangle. 

Option 3: 3 + 5 > 4, 3 + 4 > 5, 5 + 4 > 4. Therefore, the given three lengths are the sides of a triangle. 

Option 4: 3 + 5 > 1, 5 +1 > 3, but 1 + 3 < 5. Therefore, the given three lengths are not the sides of a triangle. 

Therefore, 3 cm, 5 cm and 1 cm are not sides of a triangle.

questions.question: If ∆PQR ≅ ∆ABC, AB = 6 cm, ∠B = 50º and ∠A = 70º, then which of the following is true?
questions.questionHtml: If ∆PQR ≅ ∆ABC, AB = 6 cm, ∠B = 50º and ∠A = 70º, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For congruent triangles ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC, the order of vertices directly dictates the corresponding parts.

Side PQ corresponds directly to side AB, so PQ = AB = 6 cm (thus QP = 6 cm).

Using the angle sum property in ΔABC, ∠C = 180º − (70º + 50º) = 60º.

Angle R corresponds directly to Angle C, so ∠R = 60º.

Matching our findings with the given options, we find that QP = 6 cm and ∠R = 60º is the only true statement.

∴ The correct answer is QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC

⇒ AB = 6 cm, ∠B = 50º and ∠A = 70º

In ΔABC:

⇒ The sum of interior angles in a triangle is exactly 180º

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 70º + 50º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 120º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ ∠C = 60º

Using CPCTC (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent):

⇒ Since ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC, their corresponding sides and angles must be perfectly identical.

Corresponding Sides:

⇒ PQ = AB, QR = BC, and PR = AC

⇒ Since AB = 6 cm, we have PQ = 6 cm (or QP = 6 cm)

Corresponding Angles:

⇒ ∠P = ∠A = 70º

⇒ ∠Q = ∠B = 50º

⇒ ∠R = ∠C = 60º

Checking the given options sequentially:

⇒ Option 1: QR = 6 cm, ∠Q = 60º (Incorrect, QP = 6 cm and ∠Q = 50º)

⇒ Option 2: QR = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º (Incorrect, QP = 6 cm)

⇒ Option 3: QP = 6 cm, ∠P = 60º (Incorrect, ∠P = 70º)

⇒ Option 4: QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º (Correct)

∴ The correct answer is QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º.

Additional Information

Congruence of Triangles

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they share the exact same shape and size. The primary criteria for congruence are SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

CPCTC Rule

CPCTC stands for "Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent." It indicates that if two triangles are proven congruent, all of their corresponding interior angles and boundary sides are perfectly equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles in any triangle inherently adds up to exactly 180º. Using the standard formula: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º.

questions.question: If the angles of a triangle are (x - 46) degrees, (x + 96) degrees and 8x degrees, then what is the value of 2x?
questions.questionHtml: If the angles of a triangle are (x - 46) degrees, (x + 96) degrees and 8x degrees, then what is the value of 2x?
questions.solution:
(x - 46) + (x + 96) + 8x = 180° ⇒ 10x + 50 = 180° ⇒ 10x = 130° 

⇒ x = 13° ⇒ 2x = 26°

questions.solution:
DE2 + EF2 = DF2

questions.question: ΔABC and ΔDEF are similar triangles and their areas are 49 cm 2 and 144 cm 2 respectively. If EF = 16.80 cm, then find BC.
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC and ΔDEF are similar triangles and their areas are 49 cm<sup>2</sup> and 144 cm<sup>2</sup> respectively. If EF = 16.80 cm, then find BC.
questions.solution:
Since ΔABC and ΔDEF are similar triangles, then \(\frac {AB}{DE} = \frac {BC}{EF} = \frac {AC}{DF} = \sqrt { \frac {area (\Delta ABC)}{area (\Delta DEF)}}\) 

⇒ \(\frac {BC}{EF} = \sqrt { \frac {area (\Delta ABC)}{area (\Delta DEF)}}\) ⇒ \(\frac {BC}{16.80} = \sqrt { \frac {49}{144} } \) ⇒ BC = 7/12 × 16.80 ⇒ BC = 9.8 cm

questions.question: Find the height of the triangle whose base is two-thirds of its height and whose area is 363 cm 2
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Find the height of the triangle whose base is two-thirds of its height and whose area is 363 cm<sup>2</sup>
questions.solution:
Base = 2/3 × height

Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 2/3 × height × height

363 = 1/3 × height2, ⇒ height2 = 1089, ⇒ height = 33 cm

questions.question: The area of a triangle is 96 cm 2 and the length of one of its sides is 24 cm. What is the length of the perpendicular drawn to this side of the triangle from the opposite vertex?
questions.questionHtml: The area of a triangle is 96 cm<sup>2</sup> and the length of one of its sides is 24 cm. What is the length of the perpendicular drawn to this side of the triangle from the opposite vertex?
questions.solution:
Given:

The area of a triangle is 96 cm2 

The length of one of its sides is 24 cm. 

Formula used:

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

Calculations:

Considering the side given as the Base of the triangle then,

According to the question,

96 = 1/2 × 24 × H

⇒ 96 = 12 × H

⇒ H = 96/12 = 8 cm

∴ The length of the perpendicular is 8 cm.

questions.question: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3, what is the type of such triangle?
questions.questionHtml: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3, what is the type of such triangle?
questions.solution:
Angles of a triangle are in the ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3, so (1 + 2 + 3) = 6 unit → 180° 

Then, 1 unit → 180/6 = 30° similarly,  2 unit → 60° and 3 unit → 90° 

Here, One angle is 90°, so the triangle is a right angled triangle.

questions.question: The side BC of triangle ABC is produced to a point D. If AC = BC and ∠BAC = 70º, then find the value of ∠ACD - ∠ ABC .
questions.questionHtml: The side BC of triangle ABC is produced to a point D. If AC = BC and ∠BAC = 70º, then find the value of ∠ACD - ∠ ABC .
questions.solution:
∠ABC = ∠ACB = x

∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180º

⇒ 70º + 2x = 180º ⇒ x = 55º

⇒ ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC

⇒ ∠ACD = 70º + 55º ⇒ ∠ACD = 125º

⇒ ∠ACD - ∠ABC = 125º - 55º = 70º
